title: Polynomial formulas for truncated total depth in ordered trees
source: Stoyan Dimitrov, Martin Minchev and Yan Zhuang, “BFS versus DFS for fixed-level targets in ordered trees”, arXiv:2404.05664v1 (2024). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05664v1), Conjecture 7.6

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-362667-317945-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-362667.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For ordered trees with n edges and the depth-first-search scores totalD and totalDTrunc of Dimitrov, Minchev and Zhuang, for every l >= 1 there are polynomials a_l and b_l of degree 2l-2 with non-negative integer coefficients and leading coefficients 2l-1 and l such that, for all n >= l, totalD(n,2l-1) - totalDTrunc(n,2l-1) = a_l(n) C(2n, n-2l-1) / (n+2l+2)^(2l-2) and totalD(n,2l) - totalDTrunc(n,2l) = b_l(n) C(2n+1, n-2l-2) / (n+2l+4)^(2l-2), with rising factorials in the denominators. This is Conjecture 7.6 of arXiv v1. The proof is a binomial-sum enumeration of the score difference followed by a pairing argument for non-negativity. Lean also confirms that the quadratic coefficient of b_3 is 1133, where Table 3 of v1 prints 113.
significance.caveat: The conjecture appears in arXiv v1 and is absent from v2 (10 July 2026); the journal text (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(4) 1913-1945, doi 10.1137/25M1760891) was not read, only its abstract, which matches v2. If the journal text proves the conjecture this result is not new; nothing found suggests that.
